answer: GET /Users?filter=active eq true and emails[type eq "work" and value ew "@example.com"]  -- uses a complex attribute filter (valuePath) so that type and value are matched on the SAME email entry; "ew" is the ends-with operator; string comparison on value is case-insensitive per the schema (caseExact=false for emails.value). Remember to URL-encode the filter in the query string. Writing emails.type eq "work" and emails.value ew "@example.com" would be weaker: the two conditions could match different email entries.

Send PATCH /Groups/{id} with Content-Type application/scim+json and body {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"remove","path":"members[value eq \"2819c223-7f76-453a-919d-413861904646\"]"}]}. The path uses a value filter on the multi-valued members attribute, so only the matching member is removed (RFC 7644 sec. 3.5.2.2). A remove with path "members" and no filter would remove ALL members. Do not use PUT, which replaces the whole members list. The server returns 200 with the resource or 204 No Content.

SCIM uses startIndex and count as query parameters (RFC 7644 sec. 3.4.2.4). startIndex is 1-based (the first result is 1; values < 1 are treated as 1); count is the desired maximum number of results per page (a negative value is treated as 0; count=0 returns only totalResults, no Resources; the server may return fewer than requested). In the ListResponse (schema urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:ListResponse): totalResults = total number of results matching the query across all pages (REQUIRED); itemsPerPage = number of resources returned in this page; startIndex = 1-based index of the first result in this page; Resources = the array. itemsPerPage and startIndex are REQUIRED when paging is used.

No. A SCIM error response must include "schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"] and status must be a JSON STRING containing the HTTP status code, e.g. {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],"status":"400","scimType":"invalidValue","detail":"..."} (RFC 7644 sec. 3.12). Also "invalidAttribute" is not a defined scimType; the defined ones for 400 include invalidFilter, tooMany, uniqueness (409), mutability, invalidSyntax, invalidPath, noTarget, invalidValue, invalidVers, sensitive. Use invalidValue (or invalidSyntax/invalidPath as appropriate) and add a human-readable detail. The HTTP response status code must match.

employeeNumber is not in the core User schema; it lives in the Enterprise User extension urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User (RFC 7643 sec. 4.3). Include the URN in "schemas" and put it under that key: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User","urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User"],"userName":"bjensen","urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User":{"employeeNumber":"701984"}}. Filter using the fully qualified attribute name: filter=urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:employeeNumber eq "701984" (URL-encoded). It is a string, so quote the value.

409 Conflict, with a SCIM Error body whose scimType is "uniqueness": {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],"status":"409","scimType":"uniqueness","detail":"userName already exists"}. userName has uniqueness "server" in the core User schema (and is case-insensitive), so the server must reject a POST /Users that duplicates it (RFC 7644 sec. 3.3, 3.12).

id is assigned by the service provider: it is readOnly (mutability) and the server ignores any id sent by the client on create; on PUT/PATCH it cannot be changed (attempting it can yield 400 mutability, or it is ignored). meta (resourceType, created, lastModified, location, version) is also readOnly and maintained by the server; client values are ignored. externalId, by contrast, is client-set. password has mutability writeOnly and returned "never": the client can set/replace it but the server must never return it in any response (GET, POST/PUT/PATCH responses, or list); it also cannot be used in filters meaningfully (returned never). Clients cannot read it.

No. Per RFC 7644 sec. 3.4.2.2, gt, ge, lt, le are not valid for boolean (and binary) attributes; the server should return 400 with scimType "invalidFilter". Booleans only support eq, ne and pr (e.g. active eq true). For emails co "x" with no sub-attribute: for a multi-valued complex attribute without a sub-attribute, the filter is applied to the "value" sub-attribute, i.e. emails co "example" behaves like emails.value co "example" and matches if any email value contains the string. Explicit emails.value or emails[value co "x"] is clearer.

Query the discovery endpoint GET /ServiceProviderConfig (RFC 7644 sec. 4, schema RFC 7643 sec. 5). It returns complex attributes with a "supported" boolean: patch.supported, bulk.supported (plus bulk.maxOperations and bulk.maxPayloadSize), filter.supported (plus filter.maxResults), changePassword.supported, sort.supported, etag.supported, and authenticationSchemes. /ResourceTypes and /Schemas describe resource types and attributes. The endpoint does not need authentication normally (MAY be public).

PATCH /Users/{id} with body {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"replace","path":"emails[type eq \"work\"].value","value":"bjensen@example.com"}]}. The value-path filter selects only the work email entry and replaces its value sub-attribute, leaving other emails untouched. If no work email exists, a replace with a filter that matches nothing returns 400 noTarget; in that case use op "add" with path "emails" and value [{"type":"work","value":"bjensen@example.com"}].

The RFC is inconsistent. RFC 7643 sec. 4.2 (prose) says Group displayName is "A human-readable name for the Group. REQUIRED.", while the normative schema representation in sec. 8.7.1 lists displayName with "required": false (a known discrepancy). In practice treat it as required: always send displayName when creating a Group, since most service providers reject a Group without it. Its schema uniqueness is "none", though many providers enforce unique group names. members is optional.

Give each operation a bulkId and refer to it with "bulkId:<id>" in later operations (RFC 7644 sec. 3.7.2). Example: {"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:BulkRequest"],"Operations":[{"method":"POST","path":"/Users","bulkId":"qwerty","data":{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],"userName":"alice"}},{"method":"POST","path":"/Groups","bulkId":"ytrewq","data":{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group"],"displayName":"Tour Guides","members":[{"type":"User","value":"bulkId:qwerty"}]}}]}. The server resolves bulkId:qwerty to the created id; bulkId is REQUIRED for POST operations. The response (BulkResponse) maps each bulkId to location/status. Servers must handle forward references and detect circular references; failOnErrors controls stopping after N errors.
